summary: Yukio Kotani works in Buddhist studies and comparative literature. He studied under Hanjiro Tominaga and held an emeritus professorship in comparative literature at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926) under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held professorships at Rissho University (1948) and Toyo University (~1949–1970), later serving as Rissho's president (1968).

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1963). He held posts at Nagoya City University (~1963–1973), Hokkaido University (~1973–1981), the University of Tokyo (~1981–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~2004).

Yukio Yamanaka is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).
Yuko Kamishima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo, was a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Indologist Yuko Yokochi studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen (doctoral degree, 2004) under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She held an associate professorship at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2022).
Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University (attested 2010) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).
Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She was a researcher (2012) and research student (attested 2014) at Ryukoku University.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. She studied at Waseda University (~1981–1989) and subsequently held a post there (~1996).

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD in Chinese literature at Fudan University in 2006. He served as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).
Yungfen Ma works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952). He later held posts at Moscow State University (~1966–1969), the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), and the Levada Center (~2003–2006).
Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) specialized in Buddhist studies and history. He studied at Otani University, where he also served as a professor (~1968–1987).

Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. He held professorships at Koyasan University (1965–1967) and Nagoya University (1977–1984, later Emeritus).

Yusho Wakahara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami, and held teaching posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University as an associate professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, serving as an emeritus professor at Doho (~1988–2005).

Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) was a Buddhist studies and art history scholar who received his doctorate from Kyushu University (-1996). He worked at Nara National Research Institute (~1958–1978), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1997–2002).

Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Ryosaburo Sakaki, Gyōkai Tokiwai, Toru Haneda, and Hidenaka Tanaka. He was a professor at Tokai University (~1970–1981) and Soka University (~1981–1986).
